Recommend a model structure

Source: R/recommend_structure.R
recommend_structure.Rd

Chooses one component at a time, the way a hydrologist would, each by a structure comparison (compare_structures()) on the project's own data, and writes down why.

Usage

recommend_structure(
  project,
  components = c("recharge", "distribution", "groundwater"),
  tolerance = NULL,
  n_events = 10L,
  starts = 2L,
  seed = 1,
  control = list(maxit = 100),
  method = "lbfgsb",
  cores = 1L,
  overrides = NULL,
  exclude = NULL,
  reasoning,
  note = TRUE
)

Arguments

project

A calibration project with registered calibration and validation windows.

components

Components to choose, in order, among recharge, distribution and groundwater, and optionally zones, which must come last.

tolerance

Width of the band of equally good scores; by default the project's tie tolerance (0.02 unless registered otherwise).

n_events

Largest validation events used to break ties.

starts, seed, control, method, cores

Passed to compare_structures().

overrides, exclude

Passed to compare_structures(), and so to calibration_bounds() for every structure compared; an override must name a parameter every structure has.

reasoning

Why the recommendation is being made; recorded with every comparison.

note

Write each step's choice and reason to the log as a note.

Value

A list of class pdm_structure_recommendation: configuration (the recommended, calibrated structure), entry (its calibration entry) and steps, one per component, each with the table of the comparison (with at_bound, equally_good and median_abs_peak_error), the choice and the reason.

Details

The order follows what the record can tell apart. On made-up catchments (see the large-sample article) the recharge rule was identified every time, by wide margins; the groundwater store only by margins too small to trust. So the recharge rule comes first, then the soil store distribution, then the groundwater store, each step starting from the calibrated structure the step before chose.

Each choice follows the same rule:

  1. A structure that ended with a parameter at a bound of its search range is set aside: it is being bent to fit, not describing the catchment. If every structure did, none is set aside.

  2. The rest are ranked by their headline score on the validation window, which no calibration saw. Every structure within tolerance of the best counts as equally good.

  3. If the structure the step started from is among the equally good, it is kept: the record cannot justify a change.

  4. Otherwise, among the equally good, the one with the smallest median peak error on the largest validation events wins (calibration_checks()), then the one with fewer parameters.

Zones. With "zones" among the components, a last step compares the structure chosen so far, as one zone, with the same structure plus a fast zone for a flashy part of the response (two_zone_config()), by the same rule: two zones replace one only if they are better on validation by more than the tolerance, and not pinned at a bound.

Every comparison is logged in the project as usual, and each step's choice and reason is written as a note, so the recommendation is part of the audit trail.

See also

compare_structures(), structure_set(), calibration_checks()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
rec <- recommend_structure("projects/beggearn_huish", reasoning = "First structure choice.")
rec
rec$steps$recharge$table
} # }
